artworks.title: Ajax and Cassandra
artworks.description: Solomon's Victorian canvas (Art Gallery of Ballarat) shows the Locrian Ajax dragging Cassandra from Athena's sanctuary — the sacrilege that dooms Ajax the Lesser on the voyage home. The painting is the modern image most closely tied to Oileus' son rather than Telamonian Ajax.

artworks.title: Ajax and Cassandra (Attic red-figure cup, Louvre G 458)
artworks.description: An Attic red-figure kylix in the Louvre: Locrian Ajax seizes Cassandra as she clings to Athena's statue — the Ilioupersis crime that the poets and vase-painters pinned on the son of Oileus.

artworks.title: Ajax the Lesser, Son of Oileus
artworks.description: Sabatelli's print labels the warrior explicitly as Ajax the Lesser, son of Oileus — a rare modern portrait that refuses the Telamonian namesake and keeps the Locrian hero distinct.

artworks.title: Ajax Slain by Poseidon
artworks.description: Genelli's drawing closes the Locrian Ajax story: Poseidon shatters the rock where the shipwrecked hero boasted, drowning the man Athena had already marked for sacrilege at Troy.

artworks.title: Locrian Ajax
artworks.description: A Metropolitan Museum drawing titled Ajax Locrien — reception's shorthand for Oileus' son, the lesser Ajax of the sack and the storm.

popCulture.title: Cassandra
popCulture.creator: Christa Wolf
popCulture.description: Wolf's Troy monologue keeps Locrian Ajax's temple rape among the war's founding crimes — the sacrilege that dooms the lesser Ajax and the Greek fleet.

popCulture.title: The Trojan Women
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' captive chorus still names Ajax's violation of Athena's sanctuary — the Locrian crime that turns the goddess against the returning Greeks.

popCulture.title: Ajax the Lesser
popCulture.description: Reception keeps Oileus' son distinct from Telamonian Ajax — the sack's sacrilege and Poseidon's storm as the Locrian cautionary tale.

music.title: Ajax
music.description: A Paris tragédie en musique whose Locrian Ajax loves Cassandra — Oileus' son staged as Baroque opera hero rather than Telamonian namesake.
